summary: Rockingham County, VA summit on Shenandoah Mountain; steel Forest Service lookout tower where Gerald Fawley was posted; nothing remains but a cable anchor and clearing.

facts.design: steel lookout tower on the crest of Shenandoah Mountain
facts.status_note: Former Fire Lookout Sites says nothing remains but a cable anchor and clearing; no removal date or method found

access.note: Summit lies within George Washington National Forest; a hiker's account describes a poorly marked trail and a fire road; no tower stands to climb

visit.trail_note: Fire road runs along the mountain with the summit several hundred feet above it; the trail from the road is poorly marked and the summit area is cleared (SummitPost account, undated)

events.note: Date registered June 9, 2015; nominated by Renick Proffitt

evidence.supports: location: George Washington National Forest, Rockingham County, Virginia
former Shenandoah Mountain fire tower; nothing remains but a cable anchor and clearing
evidence.quote: Nothing remains of this former Shenandoah Mountain fire tower other than a cable anchor and clearing.

evidence.supports: registered June 9, 2015; nominated by Renick Proffitt
registered June 9, 2015; nominated by Renick Proffitt
steel tower on the crest of Shenandoah Mountain at Bother Knob; posted there by the Forest Service
evidence.quote: posted Fawley at a steel lookout tower on the crest of Shenandoah Mountain at Bother Knob.

evidence.supports: Fawley watched for fires and phoned a dispatch station in Bridgewater
evidence.quote: From his metal perch, Fawley watched for potential forest fires and phoned a dispatch station in Bridgewater if smoke or flames arose.

evidence.supports: Fawley graduated from Broadway High School in Rockingham County and took a CCC position
evidence.quote: Gerald Fawley, Class of 1935, had just graduated from Broadway High School in Rockingham County when he landed a position with the Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC).

evidence.supports: after the CCC camp closed in 1937 Fawley began working for the Forest Service
evidence.quote: After the CCC camp closed in 1937, Fawley had no trouble finding a new position.

evidence.supports: Fawley began working for the Forest Service
evidence.quote: He began working with the Forest Service, a federal agency underneath the Department of Agriculture.

evidence.supports: tree growth obstructed the view; Forest Service moved Fawley to High Knob five miles north
evidence.quote: When Bother Knob went out of use due to its obstructed view of the surrounding mountains due to tree growth, the Forest Service transferred Fawley to the lookout post on High Knob five miles north of Bother Knob near Brandywine, WV.

evidence.supports: Bother Knob was one of several fire towers on Shenandoah Mountain
evidence.quote: Several of these fire towers were located on Shenandoah Mountain: High Knob (still standing and renovated in 2001-03), Bother Knob

evidence.supports: fire road along the mountain; trail several hundred feet above it
evidence.quote: There is a fire road which runs along the side of the mountain and Bother Knob is several hundred feet above the fire road.
The trail from the fire road is poorly marked.

evidence.supports: summit cleared for several hundred feet
evidence.quote: the area has been cleared for several hundred feet in all directions

evidence.supports: summit within George Washington National Forest
evidence.quote: It is within the limits of George Washington National Forest.

evidence.supports: fire season: Forest Service posted Fawley at the Bother Knob tower
evidence.quote: When the fire season rolled around, the Forest Service posted Fawley at a steel lookout tower on the crest of Shenandoah Mountain at Bother Knob.

sources.title: History of High Knob Fire Tower

notes_for_editor: No source gives a build date, height or removal date for the Bother Knob tower. The Friends page dates Fawley's posting only by sequence (after the 1937 CCC closure, before the High Knob move), so the story does not give a year. The Forest Lookouts (easternuslookouts.weebly.com) Bother Knob page holds only a photo and a county heading. The SummitPost account is undated. Brief said access unknown; now public (national forest land) with no tower to climb.
